newsitem.title: JAPAN: LUGE-ITALIANS WIN LUGE DOUBLES, U.S. TOPS STANDINGS.
newsitem.headline: LUGE-ITALIANS WIN LUGE DOUBLES, U.S. TOPS STANDINGS.

text.p: Italys Gerhard Plankensteiner and Oswald Haselrieder won a World Cup luge doubles race on Saturday in the seasons last stop at the Nagano Olympic venue in central Japan.

Plankensteiner and Haselrieder, in third place after a first-run time of 50.823 seconds over the 1,194-meter Spiral bobsleigh and luge course, made the second run in 51.032 to win with a total time of one minute, 41.855 seconds.
The Italian duo edged Austrian cousins Tobias and Markus Schiegl by 0.095 second for the win.
Chris Thorpe and Gordy Sheer of the United States finished third in 1:42.030, clinching the World Cup title after a season that included three wins and a runner-up finish in seven races.
The Italian pair finished second in the circuit rankings, followed by the Schiegls.
In the women's singles competition, Olympic silver medalist Angelika Neuner of Austria picked up her first World Cup win this winter while team mate Andrea Tagwerker won the overall title.

Neuner, 27, the 1992 Albertville Olympic runner-up who had the fastest first-round time of 51.270 seconds, extended her lead with an even swifter 51.089 in the second run to win with an aggregate time of one minute, 42.359 seconds.
Defending World Cup champion Jana Bode of Germany finished second, trailing Neuner by 0.163 second while Tagwerker clocked 1:42.574 to take the bronze.
Tagwerker took the overall title with a total 213 points, ahead of Neuner with 207 and Bode at 200.
A total of 86 athletes from 17 countries are taking part in the two-day competition which concludes with the mens singles race on Sunday.
